    Example: the Kronecker pair of D̃₄ #

    The quiver D̃₄ with four leaves pointing into the center. The simple P at the first leaf and the brick Q₀ with k² at the center and the three lines k(1,0), k(0,1), k(1,1) at the other leaves have disjoint supports, and the two coordinate maps k → k² on the arrow from the first leaf are independent extension tuples. With the trivial covering this is covering data for the path algebra of D̃₄ (DTilde4.pairCoveringData): the covering alternative of Theorem 3.10 for a tame hereditary algebra, recovering the classical embedding of Kronecker modules into representations of D̃₄.
